STAGE: design decision (record 1/2).
GOAL: pick one mechanism for coupling train-only behaviour with hyperbolic geometry inside the RQ-VAE Semantic ID assignment, distinct from the "curvature-guided prefix grouping" phrasing that already appears in the round brief and from the other 4 agents.
READ: nothing on disk was needed (no files listed/read in this step); I reasoned from the scope contract in the task: (i) Sinkhorn balanced level assignment must stay, only the cost matrix may change; (ii) the cost matrix must carry the curved distance AND the behaviour offset; (iii) one connected pathway, three switches must exist, no ablation is run.
OBSERVED / REASONING: the safest in-scope coupling position is the LEVEL-1 SINKHORN COST MATRIX itself, not a side loss. Chosen design: for each item compute a BOUNDED local-clustering cohesion from the train-only adjacent-pair co-occurrence graph, convert it to an empirical-CDF rank rho_i in (0,1) (uniform marginal, no scale parameter, no tuning); give every level-1 code a learnable stratum s_k = sigmoid(a_k) initialised at the K equiprobable quantiles logit((k+0.5)/K); cost C_ik = d_c(exp_0^c u_i, exp_0^c q_k) - beta*(1-|rho_i-s_k|)*R_c with fixed c=1 (R_c=1) and beta = m/R_c where m is the MEDIAN nearest-code Poincare distance measured on the first batch (measured, frozen -> not a swept constant). Rejected alternatives: (a) learnable code strata tied to the code's Poincare radius (breaks the geometry-off arm, since sqrt(c)=0 kills the behaviour term), (b) an extra curvature-contrastive loss on the soft assignment (violates "no standalone loss beside the pathway" and needs a tuned weight), (c) argmin replacement (explicitly out of scope, collapses level-1 usage).
OPEN: write the final answer block (record 2/2) with the full JSON.

STAGE: final answer (record 2/2). One mechanism, in-scope check done: behaviour = train-only local-clustering cohesion rank rho_i; curved operation = Poincare distance with fixed c=1 plus exp_0^c lift; coupling = both enter the SAME level-1 Sinkhorn cost matrix, so removing either changes the plan and therefore k1 and the loss; the baseline's balanced assignment rule, marginals, temperature, iterations, STE, 3 levels, codebook sizes, optimizer, epoch count and seed are untouched; off-switches exist in code but no off-arm is trained; the Euclidean (c=0) arm is a separate round, not an ablation. Full JSON answer follows.
{"idea_id":"curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1","title":"Behaviour-curvature-stratified Sinkhorn: train-only local graph cohesion as a hyperbolic cost offset inside the baseline's balanced level-1 assignment","motivation":"The level-1 prefix of the Semantic ID is currently chosen from reconstruction geometry alone, so it mixes items from very different behavioural regimes: items sitting inside dense, tightly-knit co-consumption communities (high local clustering, near a substitute/complement cluster core) and items sitting on sparse cross-community bridges (low local clustering, structural connectors) can land on the same coarse prefix, and the generative model then has to spend prefix capacity separating regimes instead of items. If the coarse code is made homogeneous in a behaviour-derived curvature statistic, the first SID level becomes a coarse regime token and the finer levels only have to resolve within-regime identity.","novelty":"The behaviour quantity is a BOUNDED local clustering coefficient (a discrete curvature proxy) of the train-only adjacent-pair co-occurrence graph, rank-transformed to an empirical-CDF quantile so it has a uniform marginal and no scale parameter; it is not a co-count, not a popularity, not a transition logit. It is injected only as a stratum offset inside the existing entropy-regularised balanced (Sinkhorn) assignment cost, together with the Poincare distance, and each level-1 code carries a learned curvature stratum initialised at the equiprobable quantiles of that rank. Consequences that distinguish it from behaviour-weighted clustering, hyperbolic k-means, hyperbolic/contrastive prefix losses and behaviour-suffix heuristics: (a) no extra loss term is added, the only modified object is the baseline's cost matrix; (b) the balanced assignment is kept exactly, so the offset cannot collapse codebook usage; (c) because the rank marginal is uniform and the code strata start at its quantiles, Sinkhorn balancing turns the offset into an equiprobable partition of the behaviour-curvature axis across level-1 codes, which is a structural property no Euclidean/argmin variant gives.","key_change":"Only the level-1 assignment cost changes: C_ik = d_c(exp_0^c(u_i), exp_0^c(q_k)) - beta*(1-|rho_i - s_k|)*R_c, with d_c the Poincare distance of fixed curvature -c, rho_i the train-only cohesion rank, s_k=sigmoid(a_k) the per-code curvature stratum (init at quantiles). Sinkhorn marginals, temperature, iterations, the hard level index rule, the STE, all codebooks, the reconstruction, the residual recursion with RAW codewords and the Euclidean levels 2 and 3 remain the baseline's.","specification":"ONE pass before Stage 2 (CPU, train split only): (1) sparse symmetric adjacency A over the 24556 Stage-2 training items from ADJACENT pairs (i_t,i_{t+1}) of every training sequence, count = number of occurrences; (2) N(i

) = the D highest-count neighbours of i, D = ceil(mean degree of A) (data-derived, fixed), ties broken by ascending item id; (3) sim_ij = |N(i) cap N(j)| / sqrt(deg_i*deg_j) in [0,1]; (4) coh(i) = (1/deg_i) * sum_{j in N(i)} sim_ij in [0,1]; (5) rho_i = ( #{j: coh(j)<coh(i)} + 0.5*#{j: coh(j)=coh(i), j<i} ) / (n_train-1) in (0,1); items with no train edge get rho_i = 0.5. Cache rho as float32 [24556]. IN STAGE 2, for level 1 only: a_k (K=256 scalars) initialised as a_k = logit((k+0.5)/K); s_k = sigmoid(a_k); x_i = exp_0^c(u_i) with c=1 (R_c=1), y_k = exp_0^c(q_k); C_ik = d_c(x_i,y_k) - beta*(1-|rho_i - s_k|)*R_c; beta = m/R_c where m = median over the batch of d_c(x_i,y_{k1(i)}) measured once at epoch 0 step 0 with beta=0 and then FROZEN. Feed C to the baseline's Sinkhorn unchanged (same tau, same iteration count, same row sums 1 and column sums B/K); the hard level-1 index is the baseline's argmax over the balanced plan; the STE is the baseline's (p_i = one_hot(k1_i) + P_i - stop_grad(P_i)), so the reconstruction gradient reaches a_k through the plan and the encoder through d_c. Reconstruction and residual recursion use the raw codewords q_k (never y_k). Levels 2 and 3 stay Euclidean and untouched. Wall clock: preprocessing minutes once, per-step overhead a few percent.","cost_estimate":"Preprocessing (once, 1 CPU, before training): sparse adjacency with a few million entries (n_train=24556 items), chunked sparse intersection counts over the capped neighbourhoods, O(sum_i deg_i*D) work and well under 100 MB RAM; measured in minutes, off the 3000-epoch budget. Per step at the frozen scale (B = 24556/24 = 1023 items per step, 24 steps/epoch, K=256, d=64, level 1 only): B*K = 262k Poincare distances, about 0.17 GFLOP forward and about 0.5 GFLOP with backward, i.e. roughly +25% of the baseline's level-1 distance work and +3 to +6% of the whole step (Sinkhorn, decoder and levels 2-3 unchanged); one extra B*K offset evaluation (negligible) and +1.3 MB of activation memory per step. No extra parameters except 256 (only level 1). Stage 3 inference cost is unchanged: rho and the offset are never needed once the SIDs are built.","falsifiable_hypothesis":"The coupling is real only if (i) the realised level-1 code of an item predicts its cohesion rank: the within-code mean |rho_i - rho_j| over item pairs sharing the hard level-1 code is clearly below the random-pair value of the same count, and Spearman(rho_i, s_{k1(i)}) is clearly non-zero, and (ii) the level-1 codes stay evenly used (hard ER and code usage close to the reference arm, no collapse). If those hold and Stage-3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065, keeping the mechanism is justified; if the within-code cohesion spread is no better than random pairing, the behaviour term was absorbed by the balancing and the mechanism is dead regardless of Recall; if Recall falls while the spread is tight, imposing curvature homogeneity on the coarse prefix costs more semantic coherence than it buys.","risks":["The cohesion signal is weak or noisy at 24556 items: sparse sequences make sim_ij concentrate near 0 for most items, the rank rho becomes near-uniform noise and the offset merely perturbs the assignment.","Hubs dominate the graph even after rank transformation and D-capping: the top of the rho scale is a handful of catalogue-wide items whose stratum assignment is meaningless.","Balancing absorbs the offset: with the baseline's temperature, a per-row offset of size m may be corrected inside Sinkhorn so

the realised plan, and therefore k1, hardly moves.","Forcing coarse-prefix curvature homogeneity can break semantic coherence of the level-1 prefix, hurting the generative model's prefix predictability and pushing Stage-3 Recall below the baseline.","Level-1 usage may still degrade if the offset interacts with the marginal constraints in a corner of the codebook, which is exactly the failure the balanced rule exists to prevent.","a_k drift during 3000 epochs without early stopping could sharpen strata into a degenerate ordering; only 256 extra parameters, but they are gradient-driven.","Single run, no seeds, no ablations: seed noise on Stage-3 Recall may be comparable to the effect, so a small gain cannot be separated from noise.","Implementation risk: if the baseline detaches the Sinkhorn plan, a_k receives no gradient and stays at its quantile initialisation; the mechanism still works as a fixed stratum, but the intended joint adaptation is lost.","Poincare evaluation near the ball boundary (encoder norms growing during training) can saturate artanh and produce inf/nan gradients."],"behavior_signal":"A bounded local-clustering cohesion statistic of the train-only undirected item co-occurrence graph, converted to an empirical-CDF rank rho_i in (0,1) per item; it is a discrete-curvature proxy (how tightly an item's neighbourhood closes into triangles) and it is used only during SID construction.","behavior_computation":"From the Stage-2 TRAIN split only: for every training sequence (i_1,...,i_T) add the undirected occurrence (i_t, i_{t+1}) to a sparse count matrix A (symmetric, one count per occurrence); N(i) = the D highest-count neighbours of i with D = ceil(mean degree of A); sim_ij = |N(i) cap N(j)| / sqrt(deg_i * deg_j) in [0,1]; coh(i) = (1/deg_i) * sum_{j in N(i)} sim_ij in [0,1]; rho_i = mid-rank empirical CDF of coh over the n_train=24556 Stage-2 training items, scaled into (0,1); items with no training edge get rho_i = 0.5. Computed once, cached, frozen for the whole 3000-epoch run; nothing is recomputed from the model.","leakage_boundary":"The graph, the neighbour lists, coh and rho are built exclusively from the Stage-2 training split sequences; the validation split is never read during SID construction, and the test split is never read at all. The offsets are frozen before any weight update, so no quantity derived from model outputs on held-out data can enter. Stage-2 model selection uses only the frozen training protocol (no early stopping, no validation-driven choice), and Stage 3 uses the very same frozen SID table produced at the end of Stage 2, so no validation or test interaction can reach the SID construction.","hyperbolic_operator":"Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature -c with c = 1 (ball radius R_c = 1/sqrt(c) = 1, the framework contract default, identical in both arms): the exponential map exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||) lifting encoder output and codewords into the ball, and the Poincare distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x) (+)_c y||) with Moebius addition (+)_c. The behaviour offset is expressed in the same length unit, beta*(1-|rho_i-s_k|)*R_c.","hyperbolic_location":"Inside the level-1 quantization step, and only there: the Poincare distance replaces the Euclidean distance in the cost matrix of the baseline's entropy-regularised balanced (Sinkhorn) assignment, so the curved metric acts at the moment the coarse SID prefix is chosen, on every training step of Stage 2 (and o

n the final frozen SID table). The reconstruction, the residual recursion and levels 2 and 3 use the raw Euclidean codewords.","coupling_path":"A single connected pathway: train-only cohesion rank rho_i and the curved distance d_c meet in the same level-1 cost entry C_ik, C is the only input of the baseline's balanced Sinkhorn plan P, P determines the hard level-1 index k1 with the baseline's rule, k1 selects the raw codeword used in reconstruction and in the residual passed to level 2, and the reconstruction loss gradient returns through the STE plan into a_k (via the offset), into the codewords (via d_c) and into the encoder (via d_c). Removing the behaviour term (offset -> 0) changes C and hence P and k1; removing the curvature (c -> 0, Euclidean distance) changes C and hence P and k1; neither side is a separate loss beside the other.","coupling_equation":"C_ik = d_c(exp_0^c(u_i), exp_0^c(q_k)) - beta * (1 - |rho_i - s_k|) * R_c, with curved term d_c (curvature -c, c=1, R_c=1), behaviour term rho_i (train-only cohesion rank), code stratum s_k = sigmoid(a_k), a_k init logit((k+0.5)/K) and beta = median_batch(d_c(x_i, y_{k1(i)}))/R_c measured once at epoch 0 step 0 and frozen; then P = Sinkhorn(exp(-C/tau), row 1, column B/K) and k1_i = argmax_k P_ik (the baseline's rule, unchanged).","observables":"(1) Stage-3 test Recall@10 (target > 0.065) from the frozen protocol; (2) level-1 hard codebook ER and the number of distinct level-1 codes holding at least 1% of the items, against the reference arm's 241/256; (3) level-2 distinct prefix count; (4) level-3 collision rate (reference: 0.065) and the level-3 refinement gain; (5) prefix behaviour-curvature homogeneity: mean |rho_i - rho_j| over item pairs sharing the hard level-1 code versus the same statistic over size-matched random pairs, and Spearman(rho_i, s_{k1(i)}); (6) the realised distribution of rho per level-1 code (should be near-equiprobable strata if the balancing turns the offset into a quantile partition); (7) coherence/adjacency/transfer diagnostics, recorded only, never used as a gate.","ablation_behavior_off":"--behaviour_off sets the offset term to exactly 0 in the cost (C_ik = d_c(x_i,y_k) only); the Poincare distance, the code strata parameters and the balanced Sinkhorn assignment stay in the code path, so this arm is plain hyperbolic-cost balanced quantization with no behaviour information. Exists and is correct in code; no such arm is trained this round.","ablation_geometry_off":"--geometry_off sets c = 0: the cost becomes the Euclidean distance 2*||u_i - q_k|| (the c->0 limit of d_c, evaluated without the exp lift), the behaviour offset beta*(1-|rho_i-s_k|)*R_c is still added with the same frozen R_c scale constant, and the code strata a_k are still initialised and used. This is the same-capacity Euclidean control; per programme policy it is a separate arm in its own round, not an ablation of this round, and the mechanism report cites that arm's directory with the same tiered numbers.","ablation_both_on":"The coupled run: C_ik = d_c(exp_0^c(u_i), exp_0^c(q_k)) - beta*(1-|rho_i - s_k|)*R_c with c = 1 and rho from the train-only cohesion graph. This is the only arm trained this round (one candidate, one run, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping, no sweep, no seed repetition).","spec_equations":"# --- graph side, once, train split only ---\nA = sym_sparse( counts of adjacent pairs (i_t,i_{t+1}) over train sequences )\nD = ceil( mea

n_i deg_A(i) )
N(i) = top_D neighbours of i by A[i,:] (ties: ascending id)
sim_ij = |N(i) cap N(j)| / sqrt(deg_i * deg_j)          # in [0,1]
coh_i   = (1/deg_i) * sum_{j in N(i)} sim_ij            # in [0,1]
rho_i   = midrank(coh)_i / (n_train - 1)                # in (0,1), uniform marginal
# --- geometry ---
exp0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)*||v||);  exp0(0)=0;  c=1, R_c=1/sqrt(c)
d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c)*|| (-x) (+)_c y || )
# --- level-1 cost, every step ---
a_k init: logit((k+0.5)/K);   s_k = sigmoid(a_k)
C_ik = d_c(exp0(u_i), exp0(q_k)) - beta*(1 - |rho_i - s_k|)*R_c
beta = median_i d_c(exp0(u_i), exp0(q_{k1_i})) / R_c   # step 0, beta=0 pass, frozen
# --- baseline assignment rule, unchanged ---
Ktilde = exp(-C/tau);  (u,v) = Sinkhorn_it(Ktilde, row_sum=1, col_sum=B/K)
P = diag(u) Ktilde diag(v);   k1_i = argmax_k P_ik
p_i = one_hot(k1_i) + P_i - stop_grad(P_i)              # STE, baseline's
# --- unchanged rest ---
e1 = q_{k1}; r2 = u - e1; levels 2,3 Euclidean as in baseline; raw q used everywhere in reconstruction
# signature
# dims:  u [B,64]; q [K,64]; rho [B]; s [K]; C,P [B,K]; B=1023, K=256, 3 levels, level 1 only
# gradient_rules:
#   encoder u_i : STE through P -> C -> d_c (baseline STE, unchanged scale)
#   codebook q_k: reconstruction gradient on the chosen raw code + STE cost-path gradient via d_c
#   a_k         : only through P -> C -> |rho_i - s_k| (256 scalars, level 1); if the baseline detaches P, a_k stays at its quantile init (documented fallback, mechanism unchanged)
#   rho_i       : constant, no gradient
# training_integration: Stage 2 epochs 0..2999, same optimizer/lr/batch(1023)/seed; frozen SID table exported for Stage 3
# conventions: framework hyperbolic contract, curvature kappa=-c, c=1 fixed, R_c=1, tangent-space norms are Euclidean coordinates (Riemannian norm at origin = 2||v||), offset expressed in ball-radius units","spec_inputs_outputs":"Inputs: encoder output u (batch [1023,64]); raw level-1 codebook q [256,64]; per-item cohesion rank rho [1023] (cached from the train-only graph); per-code stratum logits a [256]; frozen scalar beta; constants c=1, R_c=1, tau and Sinkhorn iteration count inherited from the baseline. Outputs: cost matrix C [1023,256]; the balanced plan P [1023,256] from the baseline Sinkhorn; hard level-1 index k1 [1023]; the straight-through selector p [1023,256] that carries the gradient into the encoder, the codewords and the strata. The preprocessing operator takes the train interaction sequences and returns rho [24556].","safeguards":"artanh argument clipped to [0, 1-1e-6] and the Moebius denominator clamped to >=1e-6; exp0 uses the Taylor factor 1 - (sqrt(c)||v||)^2/3 when ||v|| < 1e-4 to avoid 0/0; C is checked for finiteness and, if any entry is non-finite, that step's offset is set to 0 and the hyperbolic distance is recomputed with the clipped coordinates (logged, never silently); Sinkhorn is run in log domain with the baseline's temperature and iterations, so the added offset cannot overflow exp(-C/tau); beta is measured once and frozen so no value is ever chosen by trying alternatives; rho uses mid-ranks (deterministic, ties safe) and is uniform by construction, so the quantile initialisation of a_k is exactly the equiprobable partition; items absent from the train graph get rho=0.5; D is data-derived (ceil of mean degree) so no neighbourhood size is swept; codebook usage is monitored each epoch (distinct level-1 cod

es, max share) as a diagnostic only; no validation or test interaction is read; all inequalities use strict deterministic tie-breaking by code index so the run is reproducible."}
